verses.zh: 你们要赞美耶和华！从天上赞美耶和华，在高处赞美他！
verses.en: Praise the Lord.Praise the Lord from the sky.Praise him in the heavens.

verses.zh: 他的众使者都要赞美他！他的诸军都要赞美他！
verses.en: Praise him, all his angels.[NOTE:1] Praise him, all his heavenly assembly.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 148. The psalmist calls upon all creation to praise the Lord, for he is the creator and sovereign king of the world.

verses.zh: 日头月亮，你们要赞美他！放光的星宿，你们都要赞美他！
verses.en: Praise him, O sun and moon.Praise him, all you shiny stars.[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 天上的天和天上的水，你们都要赞美他！
verses.en: Praise him, O highest heavenand you waters above the sky.[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 愿这些都赞美耶和华的名！因他一吩咐便都造成。
verses.en: Let them praise the name of the Lord,for he gave the command and they came into existence.

verses.zh: 他将这些立定，直到永永远远；他定了命，不能废去（或译：越过）。
verses.en: He established them so they would endure;[NOTE:1] he issued a decree that will not be revoked.[NOTE:2]
notes: The “water” mentioned here corresponds to the “waters above” mentioned in Gen 1:7. See also Ps 104:3. For a discussion of the picture envisioned by the psalmist, see L. I. J. Stadelmann, The Hebrew Conception of the World, 47.

verses.zh: 所有在地上的，大鱼和一切深洋，
verses.en: Praise the Lord from the earth,you sea creatures and all you ocean depths,

verses.zh: 火与冰雹，雪和雾气，成就他命的狂风，
verses.en: O fire and hail, snow and clouds,[NOTE:1] O stormy wind that carries out his orders,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and it will not pass away.”
In Ps 119:83 the noun refers to “smoke,” but here, where the elements of nature are addressed, the clouds, which resemble smoke, are probably in view.

verses.zh: 大山和小山，结果的树木和一切香柏树，
verses.en: you mountains and all you hills,you fruit trees and all you cedars,

verses.zh: 野兽和一切牲畜，昆虫和飞鸟，
verses.en: you animals and all you cattle,you creeping things and birds,

verses.zh: 世上的君王和万民，首领和世上一切审判官，
verses.en: you kings of the earth and all you nations,you princes and all you leaders[NOTE:1] on the earth,

verses.zh: 少年人和处女，老年人和孩童，都当赞美耶和华！
verses.en: you young men and young women,you elderly, along with you children.

verses.zh: 愿这些都赞美耶和华的名！因为独有他的名被尊崇；他的荣耀在天地之上。
verses.en: Let them praise the name of the Lord,for his name alone is exalted;his majesty extends over the earth and sky.

verses.zh: 他将他百姓的角高举，因此他（或译：他使）一切圣民以色列人，就是与他相近的百姓，都赞美他！你们要赞美耶和华！
verses.en: He has made his people victorious[NOTE:1] and given all his loyal followers reason to praise—the Israelites, the people who are close to him.[NOTE:2] Praise the Lord!
notes: Heb “and he lifted up a horn for his people.” The horn of an ox underlies the metaphor (see Deut 33:17; 1 Kgs 22:11; Ps 92:10). The horn of the wild ox is frequently a metaphor for military strength; the idiom “exalt/lift up the horn” signifies military victory (see 1 Sam 2:10; Pss 75:10; 89:17, 24; 92:10; Lam 2:17). Another option is to take the “horn” as a symbol for the Davidic king, through whom the Lord gives his people military victory.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in
the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in
interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3).
Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one
and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Remember the Bible is an earth-oriented book. This planet was the focus of God preparing a
special place to fellowship (cf. Gen. 3:8) with His highest creation (i.e., made in His image and likeness, cf. Gen. 1:26-27).

- All of the different levels of creation

- celestial (i.e., "from the heavens," Ps. 148:1b)

- earthly (i.e., "from the earth," Ps. 148:7a)

- covenant people

are called on to praise YHWH, the Creator and Sustainer of all life on this
planet and related to this planet (i.e., angels).

- This is the choir of heaven and earth, animate and inanimate!

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 148:1-6

1Praise the Lord!

Praise the
Lord from the heavens;

Praise Him in the heights!

2Praise Him, all His
angels;

Praise Him, all His hosts!

3Praise Him, sun and
moon;

Praise Him, all stars of
light!

4Praise Him, highest
heavens,

And the waters that are above
the heavens!

5Let them praise the
name of the Lord,

For He commanded and they were
created.

6He has also
established them forever and ever;

He has made a decree which
will not pass away.

148:1-6 The VERB "praise" (BDB 237, KB 248) dominates this
Psalm. Each of the three strophes begins with it. Psalm 148:1-4 contains all Piel
IMPERATIVES, as does Ps. 148:7,14.

This first strophe focuses on "above the earth" things (cf. Ps. 103:19-22).

- "from the heavens" (BDB 1029) ‒ this refers to the atmosphere above the earth; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN,
also note Ps. 69:34; 96:11; Isa. 44:23; 49:13

- "in the heights" (BDB 928) ‒ this is parallel to "heavens"

- "all His angels" (BDB 521) ‒ this refers to the conscious servants of God (cf. Ps. 103:20; Heb. 1:5-14);
they are not said to be created in any specific OT text, but their inclusion here strongly suggests that,
Col. 1:16 also strongly assumes this truth

There are several Special Topics related to angels:

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ANGEL OF THE LORD

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS AND DEMONS

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELIC LEVELS IN PAUL'S WRITINGS

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELS

- "all His hosts (BDB 838; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord of Hosts) ‒ this term is used in two senses

- in military contexts it refers to a heavenly army of angels (i.e., Josh. 5:13-15)

- in an astral worship context it refers to the lights in the sky (i.e., sun, moon, stars,
comets) which were thought to be gods who affected human life; notice "a" could relate
to Ps. 148:2a or "b" could relate to Ps. 148:3 (cf. Ps. 103:21)

- "sun and moon" ‒ these are the greater lights of Gen. 1:14-16; both were worshiped in the ANE (cf. Ezekiel 8);
see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MOON WORSHIP

- "all stars of light" ‒ see note at Ps. 147:4

- "highest heaven" ‒ see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

- "the waters that are above the heavens" ‒ this alludes to Gen. 1:6-8; God controls the ancient waters

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE CIRCLE OF THE EARTH

148:5a "Let them praise" This is a Piel IMPERFECT used in a
JUSSIVE sense. It would denote a call to prayer/praise to the Creator (cf. Ps. 148:5b-6).

The "name" stands for YHWH Himself. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH.

148:5b This alludes to creation by the
spoken word of Genesis 1 (cf. Ps. 33:6,9; Heb. 11:3).

148:6 This is a hyperbolic statement
of the permanency of this planet and its seasons (cf. Jer. 31:35-36; 33:20,25).
We know from 2 Pet. 3:7,10-12 that the polluted, fallen creation shall be
cleansed. From science, moderns know that we live in a violent, unstable
universe. This solar system is not eternal. These are faith statements of God's
eternality (cf. Ps. 93:1; 96:10d) and His promises that those who know Him will
be with Him!

▣ "forever and ever" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam).

▣

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta, LXX
"a decree which will not pass away"

NRSV
"he fixed their bounds, which cannot be passed"

NJB
"by an unchanging decree"

JPSOA
"established an order that shall never change"

This phrase can refer to

- God's decree/plans (cf. Ps. 33:11)

- God's fixed boundaries of the land/sea/rivers (cf. Job 38:8-11; Ps. 104:9; Jer. 5:22)

The VERB "pass over," "pass through," "pass on," "pass away"
(BDB 716, KB 778, Qal IMPERFECT) obviously has a wide semantic field
which can support #1 or #2.

Sea monsters and all deeps;

8Fire and hail,
snow and clouds;

Stormy wind, fulfilling His
word;

9Mountains and all
hills;

Fruit trees and all cedars;

10Beasts and all
cattle;

Creeping things and winged
fowl;

11Kings of the earth
and all peoples;

Princes and all judges of the
earth;

virgins;

Old men and children.

148:7-12 This strophe focuses on the praise (one VERB covers Ps. 148:7-12,
each line assumes "praise") of living things on this planet.

- "sea monsters" (BDB 1072) ‒ this is used in several senses

- snake ‒ Exod. 7:9,10,12; Deut. 32:33; Ps. 91:13; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: SERPENT

- dragon ‒ Jer. 51:34 (also note name of the gate in Neh. 2:13; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: RED DRAGON)

- sea monsters ‒ see online notes at Gen. 1:21; Isa. 27:1; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVIATHAN

- "all deeps" (BDB 1062) ‒ this is used in several senses

- subterranean waters (salt), cf. Gen. 7:11; 8:2; Job 28:4; 38:16; Ps. 33:7; 107:23-26; 135:6; Isa. 51:10; Amos 7:4

- fresh water ‒ usually in reference to crossing of the Red Sea, cf. Exod. 15:5,8; Ps. 77:17; 78:15; 106:9; Isa. 63:13

- primeval waters ‒ Gen. 1:2; Ps. 104:6-7; Prov. 8:27, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS (water is never said to be spoken into existence in Genesis 1)

- Sheol - Ps. 71:20 (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEOL)

- Psalm 148:7-8 lists weather and topological features of the earth

- Psalm 148:10 covers all created animal life

- Psalm 148:11-12 lists human beings of all social levels and ages

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 148:13-14

13Let them praise
the name of the Lord,

For His name alone is exalted;

His glory is above earth and
heaven.

14And He has lifted
up a horn for His people,

Praise for all His godly ones;

Even for the sons of
Israel, a people near to Him.

Praise the Lord!

148:13-14 The strophe starts like Ps.
148:5, with a Piel IMPERFECT of "praise" used in a JUSSIVE sense.
It focuses on the praise due YHWH from His covenant people.

148:13 "His name alone is exalted"
This is

- a literary expression of monotheism (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM)

- a way to contrast YHWH with mankind (cf. Isa. 2:11,17)

▣ "glory" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod,
OT).

148:14 "horn" The Hebrews viewed
animal horns (esp. "ox," cf. Deut. 33:17; Ps. 92:10) as an expression of power
(cf. Ps. 18:2).

- the altars in the temple had horns (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ALTAR OF SACRIFICE

- a person's life was characterized as a "horn" to be

- lifted up (cf. 1 Sam. 2:1; Ps. 89:17,24; 92:10; 112:9)

- put in dust (cf. Job 16:15)

- cut off (cf. Ps. 75:10)

▣ "all His godly ones" See notes
at Ps. 16:10 and 145:10 online.

Here the phrase is parallel to "His people." They are further
characterized as

- sons of Israel

- a people near to Him ‒ this at first referred to priests/Levites who served in
the temple but later came to be used of all covenant people who worship YHWH

SPECIAL TOPIC:godly ones, holy ones

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide
commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of
the Bible. Each of us must walk n the light we have. You, the Bible, and the
Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a
commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think
through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be
thought provoking, not definitive.

- How is Ps. 148:1-6 related to Ps. 148:7-12?

- Define "hosts" of Ps. 148:2b. Does it relate to Ps. 148:2a or 149:3?

- How does one reconcile Ps. 148:6 with 2 Pet. 3:7,10-12?

- Define "sea monsters" of Ps. 148:7b.

- Does Ps. 148:14 refer to "praise" to Israel or to YHWH?
